name: PersonaMem-v2
ontology_notes: User-chatbot personalization eval. 1,000 personas, 20,000+ preferences (HF card later says 26,100 preferences/snippets/QA), 300+ scenarios, 5,000 benchmark QA pairs plus train/val. Histories up to 32k and 128k tokens. Preferences are mostly implicit inside tool-like tasks (email polish, translation, photo questions, therapy, medical). Columns include who (self vs others), updated, prev_pref, sensitive_info, and pref_type including ask_to_forget. Also a proposed agentic-memory trainer that keeps a 2k-token human-readable memory per user. That trainer is a baseline method, not the census player.

supersession.evidence: Paper and HF card include preference updates over time (updated bool, prev_pref). Example in the paper. A vegetarian-recipe user later asks for high-protein meals after a fitness change.
supersession.label: measured

temporal.evidence: Multi-session concatenation with topological order for updates and forget requests. Distance-from-snippet columns exist. No dated 'last Tuesday' or months-long reunion queries.
temporal.label: measured

identity_split.evidence: who is self vs others. Hypotheticals and third-person messages are in the paper as traps. Still one user and one chatbot. No companion character or lore vs lived-event split.
identity_split.label: measured

silence.evidence: Privacy-aware items. sensitive_info true means leaked addresses, phones, API keys must not be used in the personalized answer (HF card §Privacy-Aware Design). That is leak-avoidance, not social timing of a known fact.
silence.label: measured

poisoning.evidence: API keys and private strings in history must not be reused. That is a weak poisoning/privacy test. It is not a stored-memory jailbreak that later overrides a companion system persona.
poisoning.label: inferred

forgetting.evidence: pref_type ask_to_forget. HF example preference text is "Do not remember 'Enjoys modern electronic music festivals' in memory". Paper. Users ask the chatbot not to remember a preference.
forgetting.label: measured

cost_shape.evidence: Paper reports agentic memory at 55% accuracy using a 2k-token memory instead of a full 32k history (16x fewer input tokens). That is a token-budget comparison for their method, not a cost-per-turn curve vs session count for arbitrary systems.
cost_shape.label: measured

local.evidence: Code and Hugging Face data are public. No LICENSE file in the GitHub tree as of 2026-09-11. Inference scripts call OpenAI or Azure GPT-5-chat.
local.label: measured

companion_fit_reason: Closest public bench to companion user-modeling. Implicit prefs, updates, forget, hypothetical vs self, and privacy. Still a tool-chatbot personalization QA set. It would not select for character identity, lore vs lived event, cross-character leak, or RP silence.

published_eval.name: PersonaMem-v2
published_eval.claimed_score: Paper abstract. Frontier LLMs 37-48% on implicit personalization. Qwen3-4B with GRPO 53%, beating GPT-5 in that setup. Agentic memory 55% with 2k-token memory vs full 32k histories.
published_eval.what_it_actually_scores: Whether a model or memory produces a personalized answer aligned with an implicit user preference buried in long tool-use chat. MCQ and open-ended. Also scores forget requests, preference updates, and not using leaked sensitive fields.

open_unknowns: No LICENSE file in the GitHub repo listing. Hugging Face page fetched this session did not expose a license string.
Paper says 20,000+ preferences. HF card says 26,100 preferences, snippets, and QA pairs combined.
